The Scream

Edvard Munch, 1893

Oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard

Blood-orange sky and wavering lines in an Expressionist cry of anxiety.

Use this style

Edvard Munch, The Scream, 1893. National Museum, Oslo. Source on Wikimedia Commons. Licence: Public domain.

About the painting

Munch made several versions of The Scream: two paintings, two pastels and a lithograph. This is the first painted version of 1893, in oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard, now in the National Museum in Oslo. He described the moment behind it in his notebook: walking on a road above the Oslofjord at sunset, the sky turning blood red, and sensing a great scream passing through nature.

The figure is reduced to a skull-like head and hands. The fjord, the sky and the figure are all drawn with the same long, wavering bands, while the straight diagonal of the railing cuts across them. Colour is used for feeling rather than description, which is why the painting became a reference point for Expressionism.

How it looks on your photo

Photos take on the orange and rust of the sky and the dark blue-black of the fjord, with soft, wavy banding over large areas. Sunsets, water and dramatic portraits suit it. Busy city scenes turn warm and murky at full intensity.
